justification: PDF report generation (legal document handed to solicitors), flood signal computation affecting insurance/purchase decisions, new refuse-to-serve gate, Pydantic response_model validation — all liability-bearing paths

pre_impl.existing_data: flood_truth_reports table (cached results via _check_cache). SIGNAL_META dict in PDF renderer. FloodReportData TS interface. _SOURCE_AVAILABILITY_CHECKS list against internal_outputs dict keys.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Old cached reports have no data_gaps field — _build_data_gap_reasons handles gracefully via .get() on all keys. Old cached reports with 0 sources were already served — cache hit path does NOT re-check refused (deliberate: they passed threshold when originally computed).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New fields (data_gaps, refused) only appear in fresh API responses and cache hits going forward. Old cached rows return data_gaps computed from their existing outputs dict. Frontend must handle data_gaps being absent (optional field in interface).
pre_impl.external_source_error: 9 data sources each have independent failure modes — all return None on error. _count_available_sources counts non-None responses. _build_data_gap_reasons explains WHY each is None. Pydantic FloodOutputs allows None for all fields except flood_signal (Literal enum).
pre_impl.frontend_type: Yes — FloodReportData interface updated: flood_signal union type gains 'unavailable', new optional fields refused/refused_reason/data_gaps. SIGNAL_META gains 'unavailable' entry with gray styling.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If refuse-to-serve fires: user sees single-page 'Flood Screening Could Not Be Generated' PDF with data gap explanations and council contact info. If unavailable signal: gray banner 'Flood data unavailable' with sublabel. Both are VISIBLE failures — the fix eliminates the previous SILENT failure (green 'No flood indicators').

functions.name: _count_available_sources
functions.input: dict internal_outputs containing keys from all 9 flood query functions
functions.output: int between 0 and 9 — count of sources that returned usable non-None data
functions.if_none: Empty dict input returns 0, which triggers the refuse-to-serve threshold gate

functions.name: _build_data_gap_reasons
functions.input: dict internal_outputs containing keys from all 9 flood query functions
functions.output: list[dict] with source and reason string keys — fed to API response and PDF renderer
functions.if_none: Empty dict input returns full gap list with all sources flagged as unavailable

functions.name: run_flood
functions.input: FloodRequest pydantic model with address, lat, lng, prop_id, report_id fields
functions.output: Union[FloodResponse, FloodRefusedResponse] dict validated by Pydantic response_model on the FastAPI decorator
functions.if_none: FloodRequest fields are all required — Pydantic rejects None at request boundary

functions.name: FloodTruthReportDocument
functions.input: FloodReportData props object with optional refused boolean and data_gaps array fields
functions.output: Single-page PDF with gray 'could not be generated' banner plus data_gaps bullet list
functions.if_none: refused_reason defaults to generic 'too few sources' message; data_gaps defaults to empty array

functions.name: _fetch_flood
functions.input: FloodRequest constructed from intelligence brief orchestrator address and coordinates
functions.output: dict flood result on success, or raises RuntimeError if run_flood returned refused
functions.if_none: _safe_call wrapper catches RuntimeError and converts to DataField with NOT_AVAILABLE confidence

values.if_missing: Falls back to 'none' which has green SIGNAL_META entry
undefined is falsy — continues to normal render path (correct)
Optional chaining — no gaps rendered, not misleading

values.guard_at: services/flood_truth.py:1271-1288 — three-way check: query_failed vs None vs 'none'
values.if_missing: None triggers 'EPI data not available' gap reason

queries.where_clause: WHERE prop_id = $1 AND address = $2 AND run_date > now() - interval '30 days'
queries.if_zero: Proceeds to fresh computation — normal path
queries.if_wrong: Returns stale cached result — mitigated by 30-day TTL

queries.purpose: Write flood report for audit trail (refused path)
queries.if_wrong: Report written with incomplete data — this IS the audit trail. Wrapped in try/except.

break_it.scenario: Old cached report has 0 sources but cache hit path serves it without refuse-to-serve check
break_it.what_happens: User gets a low-confidence report that today's code would refuse to serve
break_it.how: Deliberate: cache hit preserves original decision. 30-day TTL bounds the risk window. As caches expire they recompute with refuse-to-serve.
break_it.repro: Pre-populate flood_truth_reports with null outputs + recent run_date, then call run_flood

break_it.scenario: Frontend receives 'refused' but PDF generation code path doesn't check it — crashes or renders empty
break_it.what_happens: PDF render error or blank page served to user with no flood information
break_it.how: flood-truth-report.tsx:430 — early return renders single-page refused document before any field access
break_it.repro: Call PDF render with {refused: true, refused_reason: 'test', data_gaps: [{source: 'X', reason: 'Y'}]}

break_it.scenario: EPI returns class='none' for genuinely non-flood address but gap says 'EPI revoked'
break_it.what_happens: User told coverage doesn't exist when actually their address is just clear
break_it.how: flood_truth.py:1276 — revocation reason only fires when epi_class=='none' AND no SES AND no studies
break_it.repro: _build_data_gap_reasons({epi_flood_class: 'none', ses_in_flood_planning_area: False, flood_studies: [{'x':1}]}) -> no EPI gap

break_it.scenario: Pydantic FloodOutputs rejects valid response because new field added to _normalise_outputs but not to model
break_it.what_happens: 500 error on every flood request — complete service outage for all users
break_it.how: FloodOutputs uses model_config={'extra':'allow'}. Contract snapshot test catches key changes.
break_it.repro: Add key to _normalise_outputs without FloodOutputs update -> test_normalise_outputs_contract_keys fails

break_it.scenario: Intelligence brief silently omits flood data when refused — user thinks flood is clear
break_it.what_happens: Brief served without flood section, user assumes no risk
break_it.how: intelligence_brief.py:1095 — _fetch_flood raises RuntimeError on refused. _safe_call wraps as NOT_AVAILABLE. check_minimum_viable may 503 the brief.
break_it.repro: Stub all flood sources to None -> call intelligence brief -> refused propagation
